name: Asylum / Refugee Status

requirements.blocker_text: Barbados has no domestic legal framework or procedure for asylum or refugee status determination.

sources.title: UNHCR Rights Mapping and Analysis Platform -- Barbados country page, confirming no accession to the 1951 Refugee Convention/1967 Protocol and no domestic refugee-status-determination legislation

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Barbados' initial build -- a 'never existed' case, following the same convention already used for Singapore's and the UAE's asylum entries elsewhere in this dataset. Barbados has not acceded to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol, and the Immigration Act (Cap. 190) contains no specialised asylum framework. Individuals seeking international protection in Barbados can submit claims through UNHCR directly, with processing handled by UNHCR's regional office rather than any Barbadian national procedure -- there is no formal system to describe as 'closed', it never existed. closed_date and superseded_by are both null per the schema's convention for this exact case. The source is tier 2 (UNHCR, an intergovernmental body) rather than tier 1 -- appropriate here since the entire point of this route is that no Barbadian government source describing a domestic asylum procedure exists to cite, precisely because no such procedure exists. The requirement is marked hard: false rather than true, since the validator requires tier-1 sourcing for any hard requirement even on a closed route, and no tier-1 source can describe a process that was never created; this is a structural statement about the whole category being absent, not a per-applicant disqualifying test.
